extracted.intended_audience: FCC rulemaking participants: license applicants, private land mobile operators, counsel, and interested commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed FCC rules and procedural requirements governing notice-and-comment for channel allotments and detailed licensing, technical, application, and buildout requirements for the 220-222 MHz land mobile band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment filing and service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be filed by specified dates with the Federal Communications Commission, Washington, DC 20554; in addition to filing comments with the FCC, interested parties should serve the petitioner or its counsel/consultant at the addresses provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text provide specific petitioner/counsel names and addresses for each docket. For procedural filing guidance see 47 CFR 1.415 and 1.420. Reply comment deadlines are separately specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte contact prohibition during Commission consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: From the time a Notice of Proposed Rule Making is issued until the matter is no longer subject to Commission consideration or court review, all ex parte contacts are prohibited in Commission proceedings which involve channel allotments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 47 CFR 1.1204(b) for rules governing permissible ex parte contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: International concurrence requirement for border allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: Canadian or Mexican concurrence is required for allotments located within 320 kilometers of the U.S.-Canadian or U.S.-Mexican border, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific proposals note when concurrence is required (e.g., Archbold, OH requires Canadian concurrence; Lampasas, TX requires Mexican government concurrence).

rubrics_metrics.name: No acceptance of competing expressions of interest for certain channel allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing expressions of interest in use of a specified channel (e.g., Channel 241A at Archbold) will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice states when competing expressions will not be accepted as part of the docket-specific summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act applicability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980 do not apply to this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated repeatedly in the synopses for the listed dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Band channelization proposal (200 5 kHz channel pairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to divide the 220-222 MHz band into two hundred 5 kHz channel pairs, with corresponding transmit and receive frequencies separated by 1 MHz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice requests comments on three alternative channeling plans emphasizing trunked systems, contiguous blocks for non-trunked and individual assignments, and digital data systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of channel blocks (nationwide/local/data) and government reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific blocks of channels are designated for nationwide or local use for commercial (private carrier) or non-commercial (individual licensee) use, with some blocks limited to data-only communications; two 5-channel nationwide blocks are reserved for Government use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The spectrum will be shared between Government and non-Government users except for the nationwide blocks reserved for Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: No frequency coordination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency coordination will not be required for the 220-222 MHz band under the proposed plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing and assignment will instead follow the proposed rules (first-come-first-served, lottery if necessary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for access to frequencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposes to permit any entity eligible under Subparts B-E of 47 CFR part 90 to have access to the frequencies in the band rather than dividing the band into specific service pools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 90.703 for details and additional eligibility categories (including not-for-profit cost-shared providers and commercial providers for federal agencies with some exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria for nationwide applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationwide applicants must certify they have a financial commitment or sufficient assets to support construction and operation for the license term and must certify they will construct base stations in at least 70 of the top 100 MSAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must also submit a ten-year construction schedule, itemized cost estimates, and demonstrate sufficient financial resources (net current assets or a firm financial commitment). Detailed documentary requirements are in § 90.173 and § 90.711.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application processing order and mutual exclusivity resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be processed on a first-come, first-served basis; when multiple applications are filed on the same day for the same area and insufficient frequencies exist, they are mutually exclusive and subject to a lottery (47 CFR 1.972).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are first screened for substantial completeness and acceptability for filing; accepted applications receive a file number and pending status; incomplete applications are dismissed; resubmission within 60 days retains place in line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction periods and license terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as indicated, licenses will be issued for a term not to exceed five years; non-nationwide systems: twelve-month construction period and five-year license term; nationwide systems: ten-year construction period and a ten-year license term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nationwide construction period divided into benchmark periods with penalties for failure to meet requirements (§ 90.725, described below). § 90.149(c) authorizes ten-year terms for nationwide authorizations under subpart T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationwide construction benchmarks and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationwide licensees must construct base stations in at least 10% of the markets designated within two years, 40% within four years, 70% within six years, and all designated markets within ten years; failure to meet the 10% and 40% benchmarks results in loss of the entire nationwide block allocation; failure to meet 70% and 100% results in cancellation of authorizations for unbuilt facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks are conditions of license; penalties include loss or automatic cancellation of authorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive channel authorizations without loading standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposes to authorize all channels on an exclusive basis without imposing loading standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive assignments mean licensee control of the channel(s) subject to other license conditions and buildout requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical power and antenna height limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed technical standards specify a maximum base station effective radiated power (ERP) of 200 watts at a height above average terrain (HAAT) of 90 meters; permissible transmitter power will be decreased as antenna height increases; the proposed maximum mobile power is 20 watts ERP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 200 W/90 m standard is intended to provide a service area of about 35 kilometers and permit a 120-kilometer reuse distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment frequency tolerance and emission mask requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed equipment frequency tolerances and a spectral density emission mask are specified to minimize energy spillover into adjacent channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific frequency tolerance values and emission masks are added elsewhere in the amendments (see § 90.213 footnote addition and § 90.209 emission attenuation schedules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of 220-222 MHz to multiple CFR tables and creation of Subpart T
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend numerous sections of 47 CFR part 90 to add the 220-222 MHz band and associated limitations; remove 'Reserved' entries and add language indicating Subpart T contains rules for the band; add a new Subpart T with numerous sections (§ 90.701–90.743) governing licensing and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Amendatory Text lists each affected section and the specific additions or text changes to be made; Subpart T contains scope, eligibility, application forms, processing, entry criteria, frequencies available, construction requirements, permissible operations, and other regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bandwidth limitations and emission attenuation schedule for 5 kHz channels
rubrics_metrics.description: For transmitters operating on channels spaced 5 kHz apart in the 220-222 MHz band, the power of any emission shall be attenuated below the power of the highest emission within that channel according to specified formulas depending on displacement frequency (fd): (1) fd >1.8 kHz up to 2.5 kHz: at least 100(fd—1.8) dB; (2) fd >2.5 kHz up to 5 kHz: at least 70+4(fd—2.5) dB; (3) fd >5 kHz: at least 80 dB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emission power shall be measured in peak values. Resolution bandwidth of instrumentation: 100 Hz for emissions up to and including 5 kHz from center, and 10 kHz for emissions more than 5 kHz from center. The highest emission level reference must be remeasured for each change in resolution bandwidth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bandwidth limitations and emission attenuation for contiguous 25/50 kHz assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: For transmitters operating on 25 kHz (5-channel) or 50 kHz (10-channel) contiguous assignments, the power of any emission shall be attenuated below the highest emission within the authorized bandwidth as follows: (1) from the edge up to but not including 2.5 kHz: at least 70 dB; (2) from the edge by 2.5 kHz or more: at least 80 dB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized bandwidth equals 5 kHz multiplied by number of channels employed. Emission power measured in peak values. Resolution bandwidth: 100 Hz for up to (and including) 2.5 kHz from edge; 10 kHz for >2.5 kHz. Reference level remeasured when resolution bandwidth changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation and type acceptance requirements for digital emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmitters exempt from the audio low-pass filter requirements because they meet specified emission limitations must be type accepted with the digital modulating signal(s) specified by the manufacturer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The type acceptance application must include information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the emission limitations specified in § 90.209 paragraphs (f), (g), (h), (j), (l), or (m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency tolerance requirements for 220-222 MHz
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 220-222 MHz band, base stations shall maintain the carrier frequency to within ± 0 .0 0 0 t per cent, and mobiles shall maintain the carrier frequency to within ± 0 .0 0 0 t5 per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording is printed in the Amendatory Text as the new footnote to the Frequency Tolerance Table for the 50–450 MHz band; see the official CFR text for the precise numeric tolerances as promulgated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart T
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart T sets out regulations governing licensing and operation of non-Government systems in the 220-222 MHz band, including eligibility, application procedures, and operational and technical standards; rules in this subpart govern in case of conflicts with other part 90 requirements for this band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must read Subpart T together with other applicable part 90 requirements; where conflicts exist, Subpart T provisions govern licensing and operation in the band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility specifics under § 90.703
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible for licensing in the 220-222 MHz band: (a) any person eligible under subpart B, C, D or E of part 90; (b) any person proposing to provide communications service to any person eligible under those subparts on a not-for-profit, cost-shared basis; (c) any person, except wire line telephone common carriers, proposing to provide on a commercial basis station and ancillary facilities for use by federal government agencies and persons eligible under those subparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed eligibility categories and exceptions are specified; applicants should consult § 90.703 for coverage and any exclusions (e.g., wireline common carriers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application forms and filing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for all radio facilities under Subpart T must be prepared on FCC Forms 574 and 574A and must be submitted or filed in accordance with § 90.127.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use the specified forms or to follow § 90.127 filing rules may render an application unacceptable for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special limitations on amendment and assignment/transfer of authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not consent to (1) request to amend an application to substitute a new entity as applicant, (2) assignment/transfer of a license for a non-nationwide system prior to completion of construction, or (3) transfer/assignment of a nationwide license before the licensee has constructed at least 40% of the proposed system; exceptions apply when there is no substantial change in ownership/control or changes are involuntary (insolvency, bankruptcy, incapacity, death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are conditions to preserve integrity of the buildout and financial/operational commitments; see § 90.709 for the enumerated exceptions and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness, acceptance, dismissal, and correction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications will be first considered to determine whether they are substantially complete and acceptable for filing; if so they will be assigned a file number and pending status; if not, they will be dismissed. If an application is returned for correction and resubmitted within 60 days it retains its place in processing; otherwise it loses its place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing order is based on receipt date at the Commission's designated office (Gettysburg, PA or as specified); dismissed applications lose their place in line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial documentation and evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants relying on personal/internal resources must submit certified financial statements within one year showing net current assets sufficient to meet estimated costs and a balance sheet dated no more than sixty days before application; applicants relying on firm financial commitments must obtain commitments from bona fide commercially acceptable sources and provide lender attestations regarding creditworthiness, system viability, amount committed, and that the commitment is based solely on the lender's relationship with the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable lenders include state/federally chartered banks, savings and loan institutions, financial arms of capital equipment suppliers, or investment banking houses. Non-conventional lenders must demonstrate availability of funds to cover total commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequencies assignment pairing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequencies shall be assigned in pairs, with base station frequencies taken from the 220-221 MHz band and corresponding mobile and control station frequencies 1 MHz higher taken from the 221-222 MHz band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the lower half of each frequency pair is listed in the channel designation table in the Notice; see § 90.715 for the channel designations table.
